doctrine: Strata are measured, not asserted (#225's amendment, point 3): membership comes from a calibration sweep of the floor tier, never from generator self-labels — #197's record is that steered difficulty drifted ~2x and a ten-task probe misread by ~2x. A re-assignment is a new dated block appended to `blocks`, never an edit of an old one; consumers read the newest block. Rates are quoted with their n because a pilot-sized cell is a locator, not an anchor.

blocks.failure_modes: All 38 failing arms are acceptance failures: 0 of 44 arm-draws overran the cap (max completion 740 of 2048 tokens), 0 parse errors. The rates below are capability, not censoring (#212's trap, checked before believing any 0).
blocks.assignment_rule: Provisional: stratum = steering band, held until campaign-scale measurement. At n = 4-6 bench problems per band per arm, measured re-binning would be fitting noise; boundaries harden when Phase 4 fills each stratum toward ~100 and the calibration re-runs. The ids listed are the bench half only — the reserve is never measured (design doc section 2).

s1.steered_at: ts 30-45 reference lines, 10-14 asserts/arm — just above d3-class

s4.steered_at: ts 80-120 lines, 18-26 asserts/arm — pool-class and past it

blocks.reading: The bands interpolate the d3-to-pool cliff as designed — rates fall monotonically-ish from ~17% to ~0% as reference size climbs — but the whole ladder landed lower than steered: g1, aimed 'just above d3-class', reads AT d3-class (ts 1/6 vs the floor probe's 16.7%), and both upper bands sit at ~0. The interior requirement holds (s1 and s2 are interior on both arms, so #119's attempts arm is not foreclosed), and never-passers exist in quantity under pinned ids for #162's no-rung-fixes-this cell.
blocks.phase4_steering: If the campaign wants a stratum reading 30-50% on the floor tier (a band point clearly above the cliff edge, where regressions as well as gains can show), it must steer a band EASIER than the pilot's g1 — roughly ts 20-30 reference lines, d2-class unit of work — because size-to-difficulty came out steeper than the pilot's targets assumed. Recorded here as the calibration's implication; the re-aim itself is Phase 4's steering decision, taken before its first batch.

s0.steered_at: ts 20-30 reference lines, 7-11 asserts/arm — d2-class, aimed 30-50% on the floor tier

blocks.reading: The re-aim undershot. g0, steered a full class easier than g1 and aimed at 30-50%, reads 4.3% (ts) / 21.7% (py): size-to-difficulty on this instrument is steeper still than the pilot implied, and the retired rulers' rates do not transfer to matching reference size (the floor probe's d2 read 41.7%; the bench's shape-strict checkers and enumerated rejections price the same file size higher). The language asymmetry is material and consistent with MBPP+ and the pool: py reads above ts at the easy end (g0 5/23 vs 1/23). Interior strata exist on both arms (ts: g1 2/13, g2 2/14; py: g0 5/23, g1 2/13), so #119's attempts arm stays open; never-passers are plentiful (g3 0/12 on both arms). Rates at these n carry ±10-20pp binomial CIs — locators, not anchors.
blocks.phase4_steering: If the bench still wants a stratum at 30-50% on the floor tier, tranche 2 must steer a band easier than g0 — roughly ts 12-20 reference lines, 5-8 asserts/arm, one small behaviour with few enumerated rejections — OR the 30-50% aim is dropped and the ladder's easy anchor is g0-py at ~20%. Recorded as the calibration's implication; the choice is the operator's at the tranche-1 checkpoint. Carried to tranche 2 either way: g0's bench-half mix skew (bug_fix 2/23, multi_symbol 5/23 against ~30% generated) wants refill rows leaning bug_fix and multi_symbol so realized bench quotas recover in expectation; the split rule stays untouched.
